name: Habitat Protection and Restoration grants
summary: Grants for protecting and restoring habitat for Great Lakes fish in the Lake Michigan basin and Michigan, including fish passage, dam removal, in-stream restoration and targeted land acquisition.

eligibility.rule: Is regionally significant if located outside Michigan in the Lake Michigan basin
Nonprofits hold 501(c)(3) status or charitable status in their country
Provides Great Lakes fishery mitigation benefits
Does not duplicate ongoing regional activities or activities funded by alternatives
Demonstrates experience successfully managing similar grants or projects
Dam or barrier projects have written support from the owner or operator of the structure

documents: Letter of support from a DNR or tribal fisheries biologist identifying benefited species
Governing-body resolution, for feasibility or design-only studies
Management support letter, if a state or federal agency seeks a feasibility study
Detailed budget on the GLFT template
Chart of work on the GLFT template
Map of the barrier or project location
Letter from the dam or barrier owner or operator, for dam projects

applicant_types.quote: Organizations eligible to apply for GLFT grants include nonprofit organizations, educational, and governmental (including tribal) organizations.

geography.quote: Projects must be located in the Lake Michigan basin or within the state of Michigan.

access.quote: Staff are available to assist applicants with navigating the online grant proposal submission process.

window.quote: The RFP is planned for release annually in the winter.

co_finance_required.quote: Match funding is not required; however, proposals that include local funding and promote community participation in the use of fishery resources will be favored.

effort.quote: Staff are available to assist applicants with navigating the online grant proposal submission process.

eligibility.quote: Projects in the Lake Michigan basin but outside of the state of Michigan (e.g., Indiana, Illinois, or Wisconsin) must be regionally significant for funding consideration.

Organizations that are eligible to apply for GLFT grants include nonprofit organizations with a 501(c)(3) designation from the IRS (or nongovernmental organizations that hold charitable status in their country), as well as educational and governmental (including tribal) organizations.
Projects must provide Great Lakes fishery mitigation benefits.
Projects must not duplicate ongoing activities in the region or activities funded by alternative sources.
Project applicants must be able to demonstrate experience in successfully managing similar grants or projects.
Project must have the express written support of the property owner(s) or operator(s) of dam structures or barriers.

after_award.quote: Projects supported by the GLFT will be expected to provide assessment of project success, pursuant to the GLFT's grant application guidelines.

documents.quote: The RFP notes that a letter of support is required from a Department of Natural Resources or tribal fisheries biologist identifying which species the project will benefit.
Applicants must provide a resolution from the appropriate governing body (e.g. a township board) indicating support for the project.
If the applicant is a state or federal agency, a letter of support from management must be provided.
Submit a detailed budget for the total project period, using the GLFT template.
Using the GLFT template, complete a chart of work form. Submit the form with the application.
Provide a map that identifies the barrier/project location.
This must be validated by a letter from the property owner(s) or operator(s) of dam structures or barriers.
